title: Persist the promo-owned core Attempt

gates.name: Python typecheck
gates.command: docker compose run --rm --no-deps backend python -m mypy src/face_moment

gates.name: Core Attempt persistence tests
gates.command: docker compose run --rm backend python -m pytest tests/promo/test_promo_attempt_persistence.py

verify.summary: Fresh independent verification passed full Attempt persistence, restart, duplicate-key arbitration under concurrency, state and range validation, migration round-trip with unrelated-row preservation, promo-only ownership, no foreign cascade and cleanup checks.
Scheduler closed TASK-043 after the T2 functional verification PASS; feature-level semantic verification remains scheduled at the FT-003 boundary.

evidence_required: promo-attempt.md#postgresql-shape RED: the promo capability package and the face_moment.promo_attempts table do not exist, so the repository round-trip probe fails; GREEN: one linear migration introduces the table with the immutable client/serving snapshot fields, proposal_count 0..20, the accepted processing_status and display_status sets, stage timestamps and unique (spa_id, client_attempt_id), the promo repository is the only writer, rows persist across a database restart, and no foreign key or ON DELETE rule lets a Photo or diagnostic row delete a core Attempt; decisive comparison: migration upgrade/downgrade/re-upgrade plus duplicate-key, allowed-state and ownership fixtures compare persisted rows and writer call sites; artifact: focused pytest and migration output under .tasks/TASK-043-T2-FT-003-W1/.
purpose: Create the promo capability package with the core Attempt table and its only-writer repository so every server-admitted capture/search request can persist one correlation identity before inference.
success_outcome: face_moment.promo_attempts joins the linear migration stream with the full immutable snapshot shape and allowed state sets, the promo repository performs create/read without any foreign write, uniqueness on (spa_id, client_attempt_id) holds under concurrent duplicates, and restart persistence plus no-cross-owner-cascade are proved.
anti_goals: Do not implement the realtime endpoint, singleton slot, deadline orchestration, result assembly, sessions or QR state.
Do not add crop/media persistence, detailed diagnostic evidence, a reliable client-offline outbox or a waiter/replay queue.
Do not create any foreign key or cascade that deletes a core Attempt with a Photo or a diagnostic record.

forbidden_scope: Display-client credentials owned by TASK-041-T3-FT-003-W1 and serving context owned by TASK-042-T2-FT-003-W1
The realtime transport/admission endpoint owned by TASK-045-T3-FT-003-W3
Result assembly, result sessions and display outcome owned by FT-004/FT-005
Diagnostic evidence stores owned by FT-007
stop_conditions: The Attempt shape cannot be persisted without a cross-owner cascade or a second migration stream.
A correct repository requires reading or writing serving_control or processing state directly.
The unique admission key cannot be enforced without a waiter queue or distributed lock.

constraints: Use the project-wide face_moment schema, the shared SQLAlchemy Base/MetaData and the current linear Alembic head as down_revision.

Models and repositories stay inside src/face_moment/promo/; the table carries the immutable client and serving snapshot columns defined by the canonical shape, including the nullable display and QR-visible fields used by later features.
Use disposable attempt fixtures with known initial state, safe rerun and complete cleanup.
invariants: promo is the only writer of the core Attempt; shared PostgreSQL access grants no foreign write authority.
Repeating an admitted key never creates a second row or overwrites the immutable snapshot.
Database cascade never deletes a core Attempt with a Photo or diagnostic record.
verification_targets: Migration proof covers direct ancestry, upgrade, downgrade, re-upgrade and preservation of unrelated prerequisite rows.
Repository integration proves create/read round-trip, unique-key arbitration under concurrency, allowed state sets and persistence across a database restart.
Static and fixture audit proves promo-only writes and the absence of ownership-crossing delete cascades.
